title: Hierarchical Multi-Agent Orchestration Framework in Python with Semantic Kernel, Qdrant & FastAPI
problem: Single-prompt LLM applications and monolithic prompt chains fail when tasked with multi-step enterprise workflows requiring information retrieval, data validation, iterative code execution, and peer critique. Naive agent implementations suffer from compounding hallucination loops, runaway token expenditures, fragile tool invocation parsing, and lack of deterministic state recovery when intermediate steps fail. This project builds a production-grade hierarchical multi-agent orchestration framework in Python inspired by Microsoft Semantic Kernel. The framework implements a director agent decomposing high-level user goals into structured DAG plans, specialized worker agents (Researcher, Coder, Critic) executing sandboxed steps with Pydantic contract validation, semantic long-term memory powered by Qdrant vector database, and reflective critique-retry loops guaranteeing deterministic goal completion.

use_cases.title: Automated Financial Due Diligence & Market Analysis
use_cases.first_sentence: Investment analysis teams need automated synthesis of corporate SEC filings, earnings call transcripts, and market news into comprehensive investment memos.
use_cases.second_sentence: The director agent delegates filing parsing to the researcher, numerical ratio calculations to the coder, and risk assessment to the critic, assembling a verified audit memo.

use_cases.title: Autonomous Software Bug Diagnosis & Patch Synthesis
use_cases.first_sentence: DevOps engineering teams investigating production exceptions require automated diagnosis, reproduction script synthesis, and candidate code patches.
use_cases.second_sentence: Worker agents retrieve stack traces, generate localized reproduction tests, verify patches in sandboxes, and submit peer-reviewed pull request summaries.

use_cases.title: Enterprise Compliance Regulatory Audit QA
use_cases.first_sentence: Compliance officers reviewing vendor contracts against strict corporate security standards need automated clause verification and deviation analysis.
use_cases.second_sentence: The multi-agent system cross-references contract text against Qdrant policy memory, highlighting non-compliant liability clauses and suggesting remediation wording.

hard_parts: Designing hierarchical goal decomposition algorithms that construct executable, acyclic dependency graphs (DAGs) from underspecified natural language user prompts
Implementing strict Pydantic JSON schema function-calling filters that eliminate invalid tool invocations and parse errors
Structuring semantic long-term memory in Qdrant with hybrid dense-sparse vector indexing to preserve agent cross-session context without token explosion
Managing cyclic reflection loops where the Critic agent evaluates intermediate worker outputs against objective rubric criteria and triggers bounded auto-remediation
screener_signals: Clean Python codebase cleanly separating the DAG planner, worker agent implementations, Qdrant memory adapters, and FastAPI orchestration endpoints
Autonomous multi-step execution report proving >= 92% goal completion rate across 50 complex multi-agent workflows with zero infinite loop traps
Anti-fake verification script submitting an adversarial flawed research task and asserting the Critic agent rejects the first draft and forces the Coder agent to remediate within 2 retry cycles

architecture.data_flow: A user submits a complex task to FastAPI; the Hierarchical Planner calls an LLM with Pydantic schema enforcement to generate a step-by-step DAG; task 1 assigns to the Researcher agent, which queries Qdrant for historical context and extracts relevant facts; task 2 routes to the Coder agent to synthesize a solution; output forwards to the Critic agent; the Critic evaluates the output against defined constraints; if flawed, the Critic emits concrete remediation feedback and re-queues task 2 (up to a max of 3 retries); if approved, the planner marks the step complete and routes to subsequent DAG nodes; final verified results stream to the client via FastAPI SSE.
architecture.enforcement_mechanism: Bounded reflection retry counters (max 3 loops) preventing infinite agent cycles; Pydantic model validation on all tool parameters.

riskiest_component.name: Infinite Reflection Loops and Token Budget Exhaustion
riskiest_component.mitigation: Enforce strict hard-coded iteration caps (max 3 retries per step) and token budget monitors terminating runaway loops.
riskiest_component.fallback: Escalate to user approval or terminate workflow with partial execution state preserved.
